question.problem: A bag contains $4$ red balls, $2$ black balls, and $4$ white balls. An experiment consists of randomly selecting a ball from the bag and putting it back until a white ball is obtained. What is the probability of getting a white ball in one of the first four extractions? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of balls extracted until a white ball is obtained. On average, the chance of selecting a white ball from the bag is 

$$
p=\frac{4}{10}=0.4.
$$

So, the number of extractions before obtaining a white ball can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=0.4.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.4).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.4)^{x-1}(0.4) \\  & =(0.6)^{x-1}(0.4)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of obtaining the first white ball in one of the first four extractions is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4\}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =(0.6)^{1-1}(0.4)+(0.6)^{2-1}(0.4)+(0.6)^{3-1}(0.4)+(0.6)^{4-1}(0.4) \\  & =(0.4)+(0.6)(0.4)+(0.6)^{2}(0.4)+(0.6)^{3}(0.4) \\  & =[1+0.6+(0.6)^{2}+(0.6)^{3}](0.4) \\  & ≈0.870\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
